Welcome! Have you ever wondered if the choices you make every day—or even the memories you hold—are truly the result of careful thought? It might feel like you’re always in the driver’s seat, reasoning things out, staying objective. But what if I told you there’s a whole world beneath the surface, quietly shaping the way you see yourself and the world around you?
That’s exactly what we’ll explore together as we step into the fascinating universe of You Are Not So Smart, written by David McRaney. Through his work, we’ll uncover how our minds—without us even realizing—construct a tangled web of biases and self-deceptions. From the sneaky pull of confirmation bias to the surprising ways our memories can shift and reshape, you’ll start to see just how easily the mind plays tricks on itself.
As we peel back these layers of self-delusion, you’ll begin to notice how things like the Dunning-Kruger effect or the illusion of transparency aren’t just interesting quirks—they’re powerful forces that shape your decisions, your relationships, and even your sense of who you are. So, if you’re ready to challenge what you think you know about your own mind, let’s dive in together. By the end of this journey, you’ll have a clearer, more humble perspective—and maybe a little more curiosity about how your mind really works. Let’s get started.
